critique: The amber/gold Form particles, black background, and fine luminous mesh detail are on target. Frame 1 is substantially closer to a single cohesive drop than prior attempts, though it still has a pinched lower lobe and a small detached particle island. Motion is the major failure: by frame 4 the object has explosively separated into a high turbulent cloud, a distinct lower cluster, and another detached speck. This reads as a rapidly dispersing plume rather than a stable, unified fluid drop.

suggestions.why: Greatly reduce Fluid Vortex Strength so the initially cohesive mass does not roll itself into separated lobes and clusters within a few frames.
Increase Fluid Viscosity to preserve a denser, smoother drop-like core and resist the severe frame-to-frame breakup.
Reduce the strong positive Z flow, which is driving the pronounced vertical stretching and upper/lower separation at frame 4.
Shorten Fluid Force Life so fluid forces do not continue accelerating and dispersing the drop across the sampled frames.
Reduce Random Swirl Z to remove the remaining stringy turbulent breakup while retaining a small amount of organic fluid motion.
